newsitem.title: PERU: PERU TO LAUNCH CELLULAR CONCESSION SALE FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: PERU TO LAUNCH CELLULAR CONCESSION SALE FRIDAY.

text.p: The Peruvian government on Friday will formally launch the process of auctioning a concession for a second cellular telephone frequency band in the provinces, an official said on Wednesday.
"The invitation for the auction will be on August 15. We want to finish the whole process by the end of December," Luis Piazzon, government head of telephone concession sales, told Reuters.

He said there were various parties interested in the concession, although U.S.-owned Tele2000 is the only company to have publicly stated its intention to bid. "There are many who consider the local market very attractive," Piazzon added.

The minimum bid price will be fixed after privatization officials receive a valuation from consultancy firm Coopers and Lybrand. But market sources in Peru estimate the 20-year concession will fetch about $100 million.

With the awarding of the concession, Telefonica del Peru will lose its monopoly on cellular telephone services in the provinces. The telecom -- controlled by Spain's Telefonica de Espana -- currently has the only concession for the provinces, known as frequency band A. It is prohibited from bidding on the second frequency band, known as the B band.
Tele 2000, owned by BellSouth Corp, is Telefonica's only competition for the cellular telephone market in Lima and the neighboring Callao port area.
